standard_prerequisites: Context span 1018-1030: for R countable, R[[x]] is isomorphic to R^N as an R-module; by Lemma countable-coherent (same chapter, delivered as card L48289) the ring map R -> R[[x]] is flat if and only if R is coherent

The context exhibits a noncoherent countable ring: R = k[y, z, a_1, b_1, a_2, b_2, ...]/(a_i y + b_i z for all i) over a countable field k, not coherent because the ideal (y, z) is not a finitely presented R-module
R[[x]] is the completion of R[x] by the principal ideal (x) (context closing sentence)
core_obligations: The context ring R is countable and not coherent
By lemma-countable-coherent the module R[[x]] = R^N is not flat over R
Since R is an R[x]-algebra retract factor, non-flatness over R implies a fortiori non-flatness of R[[x]] over R[x]
R[[x]] is the (x)-adic completion of R[x] by the context, so the completion of R[x] at (x) is not flat over R
proof_roadmap: Instantiate the context noncoherent countable ring
Apply lemma-countable-coherent to get non-flatness of R[[x]] over R
Conclude the a fortiori statement for R[x] and identify the completion
